solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: The king’s visiting LA, cutting short time with least favourite relatives? (7-2-3)

indicators.note: the letters cut into MO…W, splitting it
IN LA is literally being in LA
a short time is a MO, as in 'just a mo'

annotation.surface: A king's trip to Los Angeles is cut short so he can spend time with the in-laws he likes least.
annotation.walkthrough: THE R'S IN LA is built first, then it cuts into MO…W, the short time plus W. The question mark flags the mother-in-law joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Spouses' mothers are the butt of endless comedians' jokes, the proverbial unwelcome relations by marriage.

entries.clue: Itsy-bitsy teeny-weeny record? (7)

blocks.note: the surface hears the novelty bikini song; the setter means very tiny, the adjective pronounced my-NEWT
the surface wants a gramophone disc; the setter means a written account of a meeting

annotation.surface: A nod to the novelty song 'Itsy Bitsy Teenie Weenie Yellow Polkadot Bikini', asking about a record.
annotation.walkthrough: The song title makes 'record' look like a disc. The answer is spelt like the plural of minute (tiny), and minutes are also the notes taken at a meeting.
annotation.definitionFit: The official written account of a meeting's proceedings, kept by a secretary, is called its minutes.

entries.clue: New girl bustled about town (9,5)

indicators.note: letters that bustle about are moved around

blocks.note: anagram fodder, doubling as part of the indicator

annotation.surface: A newcomer rushes busily around a town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bustled' is both fodder and indicator. Tunbridge Wells is a spa town in Kent, byword for genteel middle England.
annotation.definitionFit: Tunbridge Wells is a spa town in Kent, famous as home of the indignant letter-writer 'Disgusted'.

entries.clue: Powder end of nose in mirror for striking effect (5)

indicators.note: a mirror shows things back to front
the end of a word is its final letter, so the end of nose is E

annotation.surface: Dabbing powder on the tip of your nose in the mirror to look striking.
annotation.walkthrough: TALC + E is assembled first, then the mirror flips the whole thing.
annotation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, éclat names brilliant display or conspicuous success, the dazzle of a showy performance.

entries.clue: Masculine ideal according to mother wears blazer (8)

indicators.note: the blazer is worn around PER MA

annotation.surface: Mum's idea of the perfect man is one in a smart blazer.
annotation.walkthrough: A blazer here is not a school jacket but anything that blazes, which the wordplay wraps around the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Nietzsche's Übermensch, translated superman, is a philosophical ideal of what humanity should become.

entries.clue: Wobbly chin is kind of sweet (6)

indicators.note: a wobbly thing loses its shape

annotation.surface: A jelly-like wobbling chin described as sort of cute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' is the definition's hedge: nice-ish is sweet, but only sort of.
annotation.definitionFit: Adding -ish softens nice to fairly pleasant, so only somewhat sweet or agreeable.

entries.clue: “Photoshop?” Ms Blanchett spat (9)

blocks.note: to Photoshop a picture is to alter it

annotation.surface: Cate Blanchett furiously spits out a question about image retouching.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spat' looks like the past tense of spit describing her speech; it is the verb to spat, to quarrel.
annotation.definitionFit: As a verb, to spat means to squabble or bicker, which is what altercate means.

entries.clue: Doctor in Gaza has Prime, local reports (6,8)

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it

annotation.surface: A news snippet: a doctor in Gaza has a supply of Prime, the energy drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a medic in Gaza; it is the instruction to tamper with the letters that follow.
annotation.definitionFit: A church's monthly newsletter carries notices, council news and accounts of village events.

entries.clue: Church attendant cross with radio playing outside (6)

indicators.note: SET sits outside the cross

blocks.note: a radio that is playing is on

annotation.surface: A church verger annoyed because a radio is blaring outside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for the attendant's mood; it is the letter X.
annotation.definitionFit: A sexton is the parish officer who rings bells, digs graves and keeps the building.

entries.clue: Unopened anonymous note certain to cause friction (7)

indicators.note: the first letter, the opening, is taken away

annotation.surface: An unopened anonymous letter that is bound to stir up trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Friction' reads as ill feeling; here it is literal grip, which is what a non-slip surface has.
annotation.definitionFit: A non-slip mat or sole grips the floor, so feet stay put rather than sliding.

entries.clue: Priest taking test initially marked down (3-4)

indicators.note: the curate takes the letter inside
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of test is used

blocks.note: a curate is an assistant priest

annotation.surface: A trainee priest sits an exam and is marked down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marked down' suggests a poor exam score; it means reduced in price.
annotation.definitionFit: Cut-rate goods sell at reduced prices, below the usual level, like items in a sale.

entries.clue: Sailor returned to deck for the forecast (5)

indicators.note: TO comes back the other way

annotation.surface: A sailor goes back up on deck to check the weather forecast.
annotation.walkthrough: The ship's deck and the weather forecast are both decoys: it is a deck of cards used to forecast the future.
annotation.definitionFit: Fortune-tellers lay out tarot cards to predict what lies ahead.

entries.clue: Check Romeo isn’t on holiday (9)

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'A on B' puts A after B

blocks.note: R is Romeo in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Confirming that Romeo is not away on vacation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as a verb telling you to find something out; it is the noun, a restraint.
annotation.definitionFit: As a noun, a check is something that holds back or curbs, as in checks and balances.

entries.clue: Team went by boat, you’d say a slower way to go (4,4)

indicators.note: points to how the word sounds

blocks.note: rowed is how you go by rowing boat

annotation.surface: A crew went by boat, which you might say is a slow way to travel.
annotation.walkthrough: The rowing team makes the boat trip the slow option; the answer is a minor road.
annotation.definitionFit: A minor street off the main route usually carries lower speed limits and more bends.

entries.clue: Censorship something Communists do? (9)

blocks.note: blacking out sensitive passages in a document before release
Communists are Reds, and something they do is their deed or activity

annotation.surface: A jibe that Communist regimes are given to censorship.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer in two, which the question mark flags as whimsy.
annotation.definitionFit: Editing sensitive material out of a document before publication is a form of censoring; split, it reads RED ACTION.

entries.clue: Profit by removing middle of sandwich and repackaging it (4,2)

indicators.note: the central letters are taken out
the remaining letters are packed in a new order

annotation.surface: Making money by taking the filling out of sandwiches and selling them again.
annotation.walkthrough: SANDWICH has eight letters, so its middle is the two letters DW.
annotation.definitionFit: To cash in on something is to exploit it for gain or money.

entries.clue: One put off by underwear daughter didn’t clear up (8)

indicators.note: the one is put out of the underwear

annotation.surface: Someone repelled by the underwear a daughter left lying about untidied.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clear up' looks like tidying the underwear away; it means to disperse, as fog that lingered did not.
annotation.definitionFit: Fog or a cold that lingered stayed on rather than dispersing or getting better.

entries.clue: Demanding a larger allotment, garden’s left with long grass (6)

indicators.note: the left-hand end of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: An allotment holder wants a bigger plot because the garden has been left overgrown.
annotation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented vegetable plot in Britain, which keeps the surface in the garden; the definition means a larger share of anything.
annotation.definitionFit: A greedy person wants more than their fair share or portion.

entries.clue: Smash mug, getting oddly upset (2,4)

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters

blocks.note: gob and mug are both slang for the mouth or face

annotation.surface: Someone angrily breaks a mug in a fit of pique.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' pretends to be a reversal indicator; its own odd letters are the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Smash is an old word for financial collapse; a firm that crashes goes bankrupt.

entries.clue: People in yeti country live among giants (8)

indicators.note: BE goes among the letters of TITANS

blocks.note: the Titans were giants of Greek myth

annotation.surface: Folk living in the land of the yeti dwell among giants.
annotation.walkthrough: The yeti is said to roam the Himalayas, so its country is Tibet.
annotation.definitionFit: The yeti of legend roams the Himalayas, so the natives of that plateau fit.

entries.clue: Dodgy feature that makes one buy into cult (7)

indicators.note: one thing that buys into a cult has entered it, so USP is placed inside SECT

annotation.surface: A shady sales pitch that draws people into a cult.
annotation.walkthrough: USP, unique selling point, is marketing jargon for the feature that makes a product sell.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, suspect means questionable and not to be trusted.

entries.clue: Range hosier rarely stocks (6)

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer in stock

annotation.surface: A shop selling socks seldom carries a full range.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Range' and 'stocks' set up a shop; the answer is a mountain range.
annotation.definitionFit: Spanish for saw, a sierra is a jagged chain of mountains, like the Sierra Nevada.

entries.clue: Sore behind starts to burn literally every beauty treatment (9)

indicators.note: the sore word comes after
the starts of words are their opening letters, taken from each in turn

blocks.note: first letters of burn, literally, every

annotation.surface: A sore backside after every treatment really does burn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sore behind' suggests a painful bottom; 'behind' is the placing instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Salons lighten hair, skin or teeth chemically, a cosmetic procedure named for the whitening agent.

entries.clue: Black tatty things, crows (5)

annotation.surface: Crows seen as black ragged creatures.
annotation.walkthrough: The black tatty things look like crows the birds; crows is a verb meaning brags.
annotation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast loudly about success, like a cockerel's triumphant call.

entries.clue: Foundation degree requiring intelligence (5)

blocks.note: the Secret Intelligence Service, Britain's MI6

annotation.surface: A foundation degree course that demands brains.
annotation.walkthrough: A foundation degree is a real British qualification, which hides that Foundation is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Both words name what something rests on or is built upon, its underlying support.

entries.clue: Private OAP unpacked summer clothes (7)

indicators.note: the contents are taken out, leaving the outside
as a verb, to clothe is to wrap around, so SR is worn outside OLDIE

blocks.note: an OAP, old-age pensioner, is an oldie

annotation.surface: A pensioner has unpacked the summer wardrobe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' is a verb here, and 'Private' is the army rank, not secret.
annotation.definitionFit: Private is the army's lowest rank, used as a title for an ordinary enlisted serviceman.

entries.clue: Downtime editor’s beginning after dealing with drivel (7)

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its first letter, so the editor's beginning is E
E is placed after the rest

annotation.surface: An editor takes a break after wading through nonsense copy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drivel' looks like nonsense writing; its older sense is saliva, spit.
annotation.definitionFit: A short break or relief from work or difficulty is a period of rest.

entries.clue: Very hot coming down from Machu Picchu? (12)

blocks.note: Machu Picchu is the Inca citadel in the Andes

annotation.surface: Hikers descending from Machu Picchu in the heat.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word into INCAN DESCENT, a descent from the Inca city.
annotation.definitionFit: Glowing white with heat, like a filament; split, it reads INCAN DESCENT, a trip down from the Inca citadel.
